framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Released models must have been tested as part of a security assessment process, and System Operators are to conduct testing before the system is deployed, with support from Developers.
what_is_tested: Security of AI models and systems before release and deployment

framework: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019, amended 8 Nov 2023 and 3 May 2024 as read
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems should be robust, secure and safe throughout their lifecycle, functioning appropriately under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse, or adverse conditions.
what_is_tested: Robustness, security and safety of AI systems

framework: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023 (gov.uk policy paper, page last updated 13 February 2025)
clause_or_page: Agenda for frontier AI risk, second bullet (position as reported by the fetch summary)
requirement_paraphrase: Countries' cooperation agenda includes risk based national policies and developer transparency, with a focus on suitable evaluation metrics and tools for safety testing (wording seen: 'appropriate evaluation metrics, tools for safety testing').
what_is_tested: Evaluation metrics and safety testing tools (to be developed)
who_tests: Signatory governments and private frontier developers (cooperation)

framework: MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1, Guidance on Qualification and Classification of Software in Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), revised June 2025
requirement_paraphrase: Claims about a software's intended medical purpose must be supported by an appropriate level of clinical evidence under Article 7 of the MDR and IVDR; software that lacks this may not be CE marked or make those claims.
what_is_tested: Medical device software claims, clinical evidence

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
clause_or_page: Principle 08, testing under clinically relevant conditions
requirement_paraphrase: Test plans should be statistically sound and generate clinically relevant performance data independent of the training set, covering the intended population, important subgroups and confounding factors.
what_is_tested: Device performance under clinically relevant conditions

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Before fielding, senior reviewers verify that system performance, capability, reliability, effectiveness and suitability have been assessed under realistic conditions; Sec. 4.1.d(3)(b) also asks for a demonstration that the system can be reprogrammed quickly enough.
what_is_tested: System performance, reliability, effectiveness and suitability under realistic conditions; reprogramming speed
who_tests: USD(P), USD(A&S) and VCJCS verify before fielding

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
clause_or_page: Sec. 3.3, Conduct Thorough AI Testing and Evaluation, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: Begin testing on infrastructure built for testing, start with low fidelity tests for fast iteration, move to more realistic non-production systems including hardware in the loop, and move into production for further testing only after sufficient non-production testing; keep production data out of test environments.
what_is_tested: AI behaviour in staged non-production environments (low fidelity, virtualised controllers, hardware in the loop)
who_tests: Operators and owners of OT systems integrating AI

framework: MHRA, Software and AI as a Medical Device Change Programme roadmap (GOV.UK guidance; visible date 'Updated 14 June 2023')
clause_or_page: WP 9 AI RIG (AI Rigour), objective 3 and item WP9-04
requirement_paraphrase: The roadmap lists an objective to outline technical methods to test AI as a medical device so it is safe and effective, and plans best practice guidance on methods to assess AIaMD performance across the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Performance and safety of AI as a medical device across the lifecycle; bias methods listed in WP9-05 to WP9-07

framework: Predetermined change control plans for machine learning enabled medical devices: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; published 24 October 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: The principle gives, as examples of transparency, comprehensive testing of planned changes and monitoring of, and response to, performance deviations.
what_is_tested: Testing of planned changes and monitoring of performance deviations

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes as a practice example that independent validators carry out verification of AI models before production use and continuous performance monitoring; also that institutions run proofs of concept on several vendors' tools to check model accuracy, and document model methodology including assumptions, limits and uncertainty.
what_is_tested: Model accuracy and validity before production use; ongoing performance
who_tests: Independent validators within the financial institution; institutions running PoCs

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Validity of an ML medical device is judged on the evaluation data, not only on how the model was developed; evaluation data should reflect real clinical practice, though how much variation is needed is hard to determine.
what_is_tested: Validity and representativeness of evaluation data
who_tests: Regulatory reviewer (PMDA) assessing the applicant's evaluation

framework: Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices: A Life Cycle Approach, GL-04-R2, Revision 2.0, April 2022, HSA
requirement_paraphrase: Presence of a valid clinical association between the AI medical device's output and its targeted clinical condition should be presented; clinical evaluation measures include sensitivity, specificity and predictive values.
what_is_tested: Clinical association and clinical validation of output

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions should keep design documentation for material models, including the form and frequency of validation, monitoring and review.
